display.purpose: Page titles only (h1 / .brand-face): EB Garamond 600, 1.5rem, tracking -0.025em; self-hosted woff2 (500/600, font-display swap), fallback Georgia.

brand.purpose: Bot-name wordmark on the green shell and login letterhead: sans 700, uppercase, 0.22-0.24em tracking, ground-on-pine, over an 11px caps sub-line.

title.purpose: Modal headers (1rem/600) and card section heads (0.875rem/600).

control.purpose: Buttons, nav items, inputs, row links, form labels: sans 500, 0.875rem.

body.purpose: Data text, table cells, empty-state copy: sans 0.875rem; secondary annotations at 0.75rem in linen-600.

label.purpose: Stationery plate labels: 0.6875rem/600, 0.09em tracked UPPERCASE in linen-600; errata variant (.slip-label) is 700 in lacre.

figure.purpose: Every COP amount, date, time and count: tabular-nums via .tabular, es-CO formatting, em-dash for missing values.

shadows.name: modal-panel
shadows.purpose: The only drop shadow in the system: dialog panels over the ink/45% scrim.

shadows.name: switch-knob
shadows.purpose: Sits the 16px paper knob on its track; no other decorative shadows exist.

shadows.name: row-hold-seam
shadows.purpose: Wax edge inside the left of a changed row/card until it is seen (released on mouseenter/focus).

motion.name: rail-slide
motion.purpose: The one authored motion: the 3px brass rail sliding to the active sidebar section.

motion.name: hold-release
motion.purpose: Change-hold tint and wax seam fading once the change has been seen.

motion.name: state-colors
motion.purpose: Buttons, links, table rows, mobile tabs, switch track color.

motion.name: skeleton-shimmer
motion.value: skel 1.4s ease-out infinite (translateX -100% to 100%, gradient rgba(255,253,248,0.85))
motion.purpose: Loading blocks read as slips being written; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Structural: pine sidebar (desktop) becomes a sticky pine top bar with brass-underlined tabs (mobile); content padding tightens to 16px/24px.

narrative.northStar: El conserje de boutique (The Boutique Concierge)
narrative.overview:
The panel is the concierge's desk of a boutique hotel. The owner arrives between jobs, does one concrete task, and leaves; the interface behaves like the discreet concierge who has already taken note — message slips stacked on the counter, the price book kept immaculate, quotes ready to hand over as PDF. Cream paper (#f4f1e9) is the ground; clear paper panels (#fffdf8) sit on it with 1px hairline seams and almost no elevation; the bottle-green shell (#1d4433) is the concierge's uniform, worn only by the sidebar, the primary buttons and the desk edges. Brass is never decoration: it is a functional detail that marks what is active, focused, or recently changed. Errors are sealing-wax errata slips that stay on the desk until dismissed, never vanishing toasts.

The system is deliberately quiet and Operate-mode dense: system sans for every datum, control and label, with EB Garamond (self-hosted, weights 500/600) reserved as the display voice for page titles only. There is exactly one authored motion — the 3px brass rail that slides down the sidebar to the active section in 150ms ease-out. The user works at a desk, day and night, in Spanish (es-CO); every COP figure is set in tabular numerals.
keyCharacteristics: Cream paper ground with clear paper panels, joined by 1px hairline seams (linen tones), never heavy borders or shadows.
Bottle-green shell as the only saturated surface: sidebar/top bar, primary buttons, table desk-edge, total card, login letterhead.
Brass strictly functional: active rail, focus rings, change-hold seam, message-slip tab, expired badge. Never a fill.
Errors as persistent role="alert" errata slips; destructive actions isolated, outlined in sealing-wax red, confirmed.
Change-hold discipline: edited rows are tinted pine with a brass inset seam until the user actually sees them (mouseenter/focus).
Every COP price, date, time and count in tabular numerals (.tabular, es-CO formatting).
Loading as written slips (.skel shimmer blocks), never spinners.
Authored SVG icon set, single 1.75px stroke, round caps — no icon library.
Structural responsiveness at 768px: green sidebar on desktop becomes a green top bar with brass-underlined tabs on mobile; no functionality is desktop-only.

rules.name: The One Uniform Rule
rules.body: Pine is worn, not splashed: it appears only as the shell (sidebar/top bar), the primary action, the desk edge under table headers, the total card, and the login letterhead. If pine would fill anything else, the design is wrong.

rules.name: The Functional Brass Rule
rules.body: Brass never fills a surface. Its five tones appear only as: the sliding rail, focus rings, the change-hold inset seam, the message-slip tab, selection background, and the expired badge (the single text-bearing exception). Brass marks state, never identity.

rules.name: The Sealing-Wax Rule
rules.body: Lacre red is reserved for errata, destructive actions, rejected status, and logout. It never appears as a title color, link color, or decoration.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: EB Garamond speaks only from h1/.brand-face. No serif in body text, data, buttons, badges or labels — the working face of the panel is the system sans.

rules.name: The Tabular Ledger Rule
rules.body: Any figure that could sit in a column — price, quantity, date, time, count, ID — carries .tabular. A proportional-digit COP amount in a table is a defect.

rules.name: The Plate-Label Rule
rules.body: Small annotations are brass-plate plates: 11px, 600, 0.09em tracked uppercase in linen-600. They name things ("Fichas de mensaje", "Precio"); they never carry actions.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Cards and tables are flat at rest and flat on hover (hover = linen-50 tint, never a shadow). The only lifted object is the modal, because it is physically in the air.

dos: Do set every COP figure with formatCOP (es-CO, ≤2 decimals) inside a .tabular element; dates and times in es-CO, 24h times in the feed.
Do render all errors — fetch, mutation, PDF — as ErrorSlip with role="alert" in the page's persistent slip zone.
Do mark just-changed rows/cards with row-hold (pine-wash + inset brass seam) and release it on mouseenter/focus — the change stays noted until seen.
Do keep destructive actions: lacre outline style, 12px separated from safe actions, behind window.confirm.
Do use the wash/ink badge pairs for every status (accepted=ok, sent=petrol, rejected=lacre, expired=brass, draft/inactive=linen).
Do keep mobile at parity: the 768px switch changes the shell, never the features; touch targets ≥44px on mobile.
Do load with .skel skeletons and progress-text buttons; respect prefers-reduced-motion.
Do write UI copy in formal es-CO with the desk's vocabulary ("El libro", "En servicio", "Errata", "Guardar en el libro") — code identifiers in English.
donts: Don't fill any surface with brass, and don't add a sixth brass use outside rail / focus ring / hold seam / slip tab / selection / expired badge.
Don't add drop shadows to cards, tables or hover states; depth is hairline seams and washes. The modal is the only lifted surface.
Don't use toasts, spinners, or any animation library — errata slips, .skel, and the 150ms rail are the entire motion/feedback vocabulary.
Don't let EB Garamond appear anywhere but page titles (h1/.brand-face); the serif never sets data, buttons or labels.
Don't pull in an icon library or glyph fonts — extend the authored 1.75px stroke set instead.
Don't place a destructive button next to a safe one, or skip the confirm step.
Don't introduce colors outside the token palette (including new module chips — extend the fixed eight-pair list instead).
Don't suggest in any screen that prices come from the AI: catalog-matched items wear the ok-wash "del catálogo" chip, and copy states that prices always come from the book.
